sample_unit: adults (18,960 app users matched to 56,880 non-user controls)

links.outcome: Dermatological claims for (pre)malignant and benign lesions in app users versus matched controls
links.effect: App users had more (pre)malignant claims (6.0% vs 4.6%, OR 1.3) and more benign tumor/nevi claims (5.9% vs 1.7%, OR 3.7). Cost per additional (pre)malignancy detected was €2567.
links.quote: Here we report that mHealth-users had more claims for (pre)malignant skin lesions than controls (6.0% vs 4.6%, OR 1.3 (95% CI 1.2-1.4)) and also a more than threefold higher risk of claims for benign skin tumors and nevi (5.9% vs 1.7%, OR 3.7 (95% CI 3.4-4.1)).

screen.reason: Retrospective pragmatic evaluation of a real-world population deployment of a patient-facing AI skin cancer detection app, assessing its impact on dermatological healthcare utilization and cost-effectiveness.
